questions.question: The phenomenon of electromagnetic induction is

options.explanation: A rheostat is used to vary resistance and does not protect circuits.

questions.explanation: A fuse is a safety device that melts and breaks the circuit when the current exceeds a safe limit, protecting the appliances and wiring from damage caused by overloading or short-circuiting.
questions.hint: Think about the device that protects electrical circuits from excessive current.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: A straight conductor carrying current in the north direction is placed in a magnetic field pointing towards the east. The conductor will experience a force in which direction?

options.text: Upwards
options.explanation: The force on the conductor will be upwards as per Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.

options.text: Downwards
options.explanation: The force is not downwards; it is upwards.

options.text: East
options.explanation: The force is not in the direction of the magnetic field.

options.text: West
options.explanation: The force is not in the direction opposite to the magnetic field.

questions.explanation: Using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: The forefinger points east (magnetic field), the middle finger points north (current), and the thumb will point upwards, indicating the direction of the force.
questions.hint: Apply Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to determine the direction of the force.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: What is the S.I. unit of magnetic field strength?

options.text: Ampere
options.explanation: Ampere is the S.I. unit of electric current, not magnetic field strength.

options.text: Volt
options.explanation: Volt is the S.I. unit of electric potential difference, not magnetic field strength.

options.text: Tesla
options.explanation: Tesla (T) is the correct S.I. unit for magnetic field strength.

options.text: Ohm
options.explanation: Ohm is the S.I. unit of electrical resistance, not magnetic field strength.

questions.explanation: The S.I. unit for magnetic field strength (or magnetic flux density) is Tesla (T).
questions.hint: Recall the unit named after a scientist associated with electromagnetism.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about magnetic field lines is incorrect?

options.text: They emerge from the North pole and merge into the South pole.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about magnetic field lines.

options.text: They do not intersect each other.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about magnetic field lines.

options.text: The density of field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about magnetic field lines.

options.text: They form open curves.
options.explanation: This is an incorrect statement as magnetic field lines form closed loops.

questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops, extending from the North pole to the South pole outside the magnet, and from the South pole to the North pole inside the magnet. Therefore, they do not form open curves.
questions.hint: Magnetic field lines are always continuous and closed loops.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: An electric motor converts:

options.text: Mechanical energy into electrical energy.
options.explanation: This describes a generator, not a motor.

options.text: Electrical energy into mechanical energy.
options.explanation: This is the correct function of an electric motor.

options.text: Chemical energy into electrical energy.
options.explanation: This describes a battery, not a motor.

options.text: Electrical energy into light energy.
options.explanation: This describes a bulb, not a motor.

questions.explanation: An electric motor operates on the principle of the magnetic effect of electric current, converting the supplied electrical energy into mechanical energy (rotation).
questions.hint: Think about the primary function of an electric motor.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: According to Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, what does the forefinger represent?

options.text: Direction of current
options.explanation: The middle finger represents the direction of current.

options.text: Direction of force
options.explanation: The thumb represents the direction of force.

options.text: Direction of magnetic field
options.explanation: The forefinger represents the direction of the magnetic field.

options.text: Direction of motion
options.explanation: The thumb represents the direction of motion/force.

questions.explanation: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, the thumb points to the direction of force/motion, the forefinger points to the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger points to the direction of the current.
questions.hint: Recall the mnemonic for Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Thumb (Force), Forefinger (Field), Middle finger (Current).
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: The essential difference between an AC generator and a DC generator is that:

options.text: AC generator has an electromagnet while a DC generator has a permanent magnet.
options.explanation: This is not the essential difference.

options.text: DC generator will generate a higher voltage.
options.explanation: Voltage depends on other factors, not the type of generator.

options.text: AC generator has slip rings while a DC generator has a commutator.
options.explanation: This is the correct structural difference.

options.text: AC generator rotates faster than a DC generator.
options.explanation: Rotation speed is not the essential difference.

questions.explanation: The main structural difference between an AC generator and a DC generator lies in their output contact mechanisms. An AC generator uses two slip rings to collect current, resulting in alternating current. A DC generator uses a split-ring commutator which reverses the current direction every half rotation, resulting in direct current.
questions.hint: Consider the components used for current collection in AC and DC generators.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: A current-carrying conductor is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. If the direction of current is reversed, what will happen to the force experienced by the conductor?

options.text: The force will become zero.
options.explanation: The force does not become zero; it reverses direction.

options.text: The force will double in magnitude.
options.explanation: The magnitude of the force remains the same; only the direction changes.

options.text: The direction of the force will be reversed.
options.explanation: Reversing the current reverses the direction of the force.

options.text: The magnitude of the force will decrease.
options.explanation: The magnitude of the force remains unchanged.

questions.explanation: According to Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, the direction of the force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is perpendicular to both the direction of the current and the magnetic field. If the direction of the current is reversed, while the magnetic field remains the same, the direction of the force will also reverse.
questions.hint: Use Fleming's Left-Hand Rule to determine the effect of reversing the current direction.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: Why is an alternating current (AC) preferred over direct current (DC) for long-distance transmission of electrical energy?

options.text: AC can be easily converted to DC.
options.explanation: While true, this is not the primary reason for preferring AC in transmission.

options.text: AC can be transmitted with less power loss at high voltages.
options.explanation: This is the main reason for preferring AC in long-distance transmission.

options.text: AC generators are more efficient than DC generators.
options.explanation: Efficiency of generators is not the primary reason for preferring AC in transmission.

options.text: AC current is safer than DC current.
options.explanation: Safety is not the primary reason for preferring AC in transmission.

questions.explanation: AC can be easily stepped up or stepped down using transformers. By stepping up the voltage for transmission, the current is reduced (P=VI), which significantly minimizes power loss (P=I²R) in transmission lines over long distances. DC cannot be easily stepped up or down efficiently for this purpose.
questions.hint: Consider the efficiency of transmission and the role of transformers.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the strength of the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying solenoid?

options.text: Number of turns in the coil.
options.explanation: This directly affects the magnetic field strength.

options.text: Current flowing through the coil.
options.explanation: This directly affects the magnetic field strength.

options.text: Nature of the core material inside the solenoid.
options.explanation: This directly affects the magnetic field strength.

options.text: Diameter of the wire used in the coil.
options.explanation: This does not directly affect the magnetic field strength.

questions.explanation: The strength of the magnetic field inside a solenoid primarily depends on the number of turns per unit length (N/L), the current (I) flowing through it, and the nature of the core material (its permeability). The diameter of the wire mainly affects the resistance of the coil, which in turn affects the current for a given voltage, but it does not directly determine the magnetic field strength for a specified current and number of turns.
questions.hint: Consider the factors that directly influence the magnetic field strength in a solenoid.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: Assertion (A): A compass needle is deflected when brought near a current-carrying conductor. Reason (R): The current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Oersted's experiment demonstrated that an electric current produces a magnetic field around it. A compass needle is a small magnet, and it gets deflected when placed in a magnetic field. Therefore, the magnetic field produced by the current-carrying conductor causes the deflection of the compass needle.
questions.hint: Recall Oersted's experiment and the properties of magnetic fields.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: A student is experimenting with an electric motor. He observes that the coil in the motor rotates when current is passed through it. He wants to increase the speed of rotation of the coil. Which of the following changes would be most effective in achieving this?

options.text: Increasing the resistance of the coil.
options.explanation: Increasing resistance reduces current, which decreases torque and speed.

options.text: Decreasing the strength of the magnetic field.
options.explanation: Decreasing the magnetic field strength reduces torque and speed.

options.text: Increasing the number of turns in the coil.
options.explanation: Increasing the number of turns increases torque, thereby increasing speed.

options.text: Using a weaker battery.
options.explanation: A weaker battery reduces current, which decreases torque and speed.

questions.explanation: The turning effect (torque) in an electric motor depends on the number of turns in the coil, the strength of the magnetic field, and the current. Increasing the number of turns in the coil increases the torque, thereby increasing the speed of rotation.
questions.hint: Consider the factors that affect the torque in an electric motor.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about magnetic field lines is INCORRECT?

options.text: They originate from the North pole and merge at the South pole.
options.explanation: This is a correct property of magnetic field lines.

options.text: They do not intersect each other.
options.explanation: This is a correct property of magnetic field lines.

options.text: The density of field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
options.explanation: This is a correct property of magnetic field lines.

options.text: They form open curves, starting from the North pole and ending at the South pole.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because magnetic field lines form closed loops.

questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops, extending from the North pole to the South pole outside the magnet and from the South pole to the North pole inside the magnet. Therefore, the statement that they form open curves is incorrect.
questions.hint: Magnetic field lines are always continuous and form closed loops.
questions.subject: maha10-physics

questions.question: An electric motor works on the principle that a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force. To determine the direction of this force, which of the following rules is applied?

options.text: Maxwell's Right-Hand Thumb Rule
options.explanation: This rule is for the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire.

options.text: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule
options.explanation: This rule is for the direction of induced current in a generator.

options.text: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
options.explanation: This rule is fundamental to the working of an electric motor.

options.text: Lenz's Law
options.explanation: Lenz's Law relates to the direction of induced current opposing the change in magnetic flux.

questions.explanation: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is used to determine the direction of force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field. The thumb points in the direction of force, the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger in the direction of the current.
questions.hint: This rule is specifically used for electric motors.
questions.subject: maha10-physics
